2.text: Expansion of the Reindeer Chukchee and New Tribute. — As one

3.text: reason for the introduction of the new tribute among the Reindeer Chukchee,

4.text: Maydell cited the circumstance that from the time of the cessation of hostilities

5.text: they were slowly but incessantly moving westward and southward. In the

6.text: time of the Russian war their western frontier was somewhere west of the

7.text: Chaun River and on the upper courses of both Anui Rivers. In the thirties

8.text: of the nineteenth century their camps extended to the Large Baranikha River,

9.text: although this country was considered as having belonged, from times of old,

10.text: to the Yukaghir of the Anui. In the fifties of the nineteenth century the

11.text: Chukchee proceeded first to the Labugen, then to the Pohinden, both affluents

12.text: of the Dry Anui River. Their onward movement was connected with the

13.text: vanishing of the Yukaghir. These last died out, or receded to the Kolyma,

14.text: because the wild-reindeer herds were turned away from their yearly migratory

15.text: route across the Anui and Kolyma Rivers. This last circumstance was probably

16.text: due to the increase of the Chukchee herds. Thus the pacification of the

17.text: country proved unfavorable to the lower material culture of the Yukaghir

18.text: hunters, and quite favorable to the nomad culture of the Chukchee, which

19.text: was higher than that of the Yukaghir, though in other respects the Chukchee

21.text: In the end of the fifties of the nineteenth century the foremost Chukchee

22.text: camps crossed the Kolyma River to the west, and were approaching the

23.text: Omolon River on the south. All this territory was formerly occupied by the

24.text: Yukaghir, who were already half extinct; but the Chukchee were conscious

25.text: that the land was not theirs, and considered themselves under obligation to

26.text: pay at least something for those new pastures. Maydell asserts that he was

27.text: the first to give permission to the Chukchee to cross the Kolyma River, but

28.text: this is not the case. Some Chukchee crossed the Kolyma as early as 1859

29.text: with the permission of one of the predecessors of Maydell. Another party

30.text: crossed the Kolyma River in 1866. As to the tribute, Maydell had good

31.text: sense enough to abolish the former standard of one red fox per head as too

32.text: high, and not easily obtained by the reindeer-breeding Chukchee on their

33.text: treeless tundras. He established a new standard, low in price and easily

34.text: procured, — one reindeer-skin scraped and worked into soft leather. A consider-

35.text: able number of such skins are prepared by all the tribes of the country.

36.text: Some of them are used for clothing; others are exported to Yakutsk, there

37.text: to be used by the Yakut also for clothing. Each Chukchee family has,

38.text: besides, a number of spare reindeer-skins. Thus the women are able at all

39.text: times to prepare soft curried leather. Still the collecting of soft skins as tribute

40.text: proved a failure. Many of the Chukchee brought skins of bad quality or none

41.text: at all; and the deficiency was paid by Amraˊwkurg̣ɪn and the other chiefs.
